paper_metadata.title: Effect of Re addition on microstructure and mechanical properties of Ir–Rh alloy

evidence.quote: Homogenization heat treatment was carried out by SWSL-2100/14 type vacuum tungsten wire furnace. The heat treatment temperature was set at 1400 ◦C with a holding time of 6 h. The heating protocol involved ramping from room temperature to 800 ◦C at a rate of 10 ◦C per minute, followed by a more gradual increase from 800 ◦C to the target temperature of 1400 ◦C at a rate of 5 ◦C per minute. Upon completion of the heat treatment, the sample was cooled at a controlled rate of 10 ◦C per minute down to 800 ◦C, after which it was furnace-cooled to room temperature.

evidence.section: 4.2. Re effect on the strengthening mechanism
evidence.quote: Ir–7Rh alloys show a significant increase in dislocation density during plastic deformation, resulting in the formation of high-density dislocation regions. The dislocation lines within these regions exhibit dislocation tangles.

Rhenium (Re) is an extremely critical element for nickel- and cobalt-based superalloys, which can significantly improve the low-temperature brittleness, machinability, and enhance creep resistance through solid-solution strengthening mechanism.

evidence.section: 4.1. Re effect on the dendritic structures
evidence.quote: The introduction of rhenium (Re) promotes the formation of dendritic structure, which is primarily attributed to the enhanced constitutional supercooling effect induced by Re addition

evidence.section: 4.2. Re effect on the strengthening mechanism
evidence.quote: the introduction of the dislocation pinning effect further enhances the yield strength of the material and strengthens the mechanical properties and microstructural stability of the alloy

evidence.section: 4.2. Re effect on the strengthening mechanism
evidence.quote: The addition of rhenium leads to grain refinement, increasing the grain boundary area, enrichment of rhenium at the solid-liquid interface improves melt supercooling, promotes nucleation and inhibits grain growth. Increased grain boundaries impede the movement of dislocations and improve microstructural stability.
Thus, Re addition facilitates the transition of the fracture mechanism from brittle to ductile.
